title: PSG4-ELASTIC-THIRD: adaptive base yields a negative source correction at unchanged time

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2N), L=log2n, the ONE PSG4-ELASTIC-THIRD program in proof.md uses the explicit exhaustive branch for n<256 and otherwise the exact C4096 list instrument with delta(v)=min{d>=0:20*2^d>=21*(2v+6)}. Compute ell_base=ceil(log2n), g_base as the largest integer with g_base^8*ell_base^3<=n^4, and for each trial R set u=min(R,max(1,floor(R/3)+floor(7g_base/4))). Use the first exact profile with2S_u(R)>=n; recompute q0,all decoder/precision parameters and BOTH literal acquisition and weighted-work caps. It recovers the whole secret from independent ideal copies with unconditional success at least1-2^-8>2/3. Jointly on EVERY branch including failed searches, rejected/discarded copies, wrong labels, both aborts, initialization and cleanup, time T is O(2^((3/4)sqrt(nL)+sqrt(n)L^(-3/8))) with exact growth index1/2. All outside constants are absolute independent of N,s,outcomes. Source acquisition, all bit arithmetic, uniform circuit generation, full indexed-address fees, measurements, resets, preprocessing, failed work, complete decoder and cleanup are paid jointly with both spaces, source cap, unconditional full-secret success and clean fraction0 for the same selected configuration.

No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
